To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ConCavity is the first ligand binding site prediction algorithm to integrate evolutionary sequence conservation estimates and 3D structure-based methods for predicting protein ligand binding sites; and 2) ConCavity substantially improves upon existing methods for predicting both 3D protein ligand binding pockets (by 20% in terms of the AUC metric) and individual ligand-binding residues (by 30% in terms of sensitivity).

(a) ConCavity outperforms existing approaches for predicting ligand binding sites in proteins; (b) ConCavity can be used to accurately predict catalytic sites; (c) combining evolutionary sequence conservation and structure-based methods improves upon either method alone; (d) evolutionary sequence conservation is not a good predictor of ligand binding sites, but is a good predictor of catalytic residues; (e) ConCavity is useful in predicting drug binding sites in proteins.
